340164.title: Eulerian edge-refinement conjecture for sphere embeddings
340164.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-sphere with $d\geq 2$ and let $H$ be a $(d+1)$-sphere containing $G$ as a subgraph. An **edge refinement** inserts a vertex into an edge and joins it to the common neighbors of the edge's endpoints. A graph is **Eulerian** when the relevant simplex degrees are even.

**Eulerian edge-refinement conjecture.** It is possible to edge refine $H$, using only edges different from those of $G$, so that the modified $H$ becomes Eulerian.

The conjecture is proposed as a sufficient condition for the sphere coloring conjecture: an Eulerian host would provide a coloring of the embedded sphere with $d+1$ or $d+2$ colors. The source gives no resolution and notes that the higher-dimensional cases remain to be investigated.

340164.precise_remaining_obligation: Need either an invariant preventing all permitted refinement sequences, or a full relative Eulerian-refinement construction. A finite unsuccessful refinement sweep proves neither.

340201.title: Banica's universal flat matrix model conjecture for quantum permutation groups
340201.literal_statement:
Let $S_N^+$ be the quantum permutation group, and let $X_N$ be the compact space of $N\times N$ matrices $P=(P_{ij})$ whose entries are rank-one projections in $M_N(\mathbb C)$ satisfying

$$
\sum_jP_{ij}=1=\sum_iP_{ij}.
$$

The universal flat matrix model is the representation

$$
\pi:\mathcal A(S_N^+)\to M_N(C(X_N)),\qquad \pi(u_{ij})=\{P\mapsto P_{ij}\}.
$$

A representation is **faithful** when it is injective, and **inner faithful** when its kernel contains no non-trivial Hopf $\ast$-ideals. **Universal flat matrix model conjecture.** The universal flat matrix model is faithful for $N=4$ and inner faithful for $N\geq5$. The conjecture is attributed to Banica; the source does not provide evidence of resolution.
340201.review_depth: Conjecture 4.3, Remark 4.4, Proposition 4.6, Proposition 4.8 and Corollary 4.9 of source.
340201.mathematical_attempts: Faithfulness at N=4 is already known; source proves inner faithfulness for N<=5 and N>=10. No finite combinatorial certificate for the remaining N=6,7,8,9 found.
340201.precise_remaining_obligation: Need inner faithfulness at each of N=6,7,8,9, or a nonzero Hopf ideal witnessing failure. Testing rank-one projection examples is not a proof.
340201.novelty_status: No eligible new result claimed; bounded searches do not certify absence of prior work.

340298.title: Mountain-end anchored packing conjecture
340298.literal_statement:
Consider a mountain permutation on the points, and suppose it starts with $m$ and ends with $(m-1,m-2,\ldots,1)$ for some $m\leq n$. Let $k$ be the proportion of the rectangular region with opposite vertices $P_1$ and $(x_{n-m+1},1)$ that can be filled, where $k>\frac12$. **Mountain-end conjecture.** Under these assumptions, one can fill at least

$$
\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2\left(m+\frac{1}{2k-1}\right)}
$$

of the entire square. This claim is proposed as a strengthening for mountain permutations and would imply the lower bound $\frac12+\frac{1}{2n}$ for their optimal area; the source proves only the weaker half-area bound for mountain permutations.

340298.precise_remaining_obligation: Either a substantive geometric obstruction with an exact packing optimum, or a new full-scope argument beyond the source reduction is required; hypothesis k is an attainable proportion, hence k<=1.

340518.title: The monotonicity conjecture for exceptional-word ratios
340518.literal_statement:
For each positive integer $m$, let $\mathcal E_m$ be the set of exceptional normalized words of length $m$, and let $\mathcal{NW}_m$ be the set of normalized words of length $m$. Here, a word is **exceptional** when its hare-fertility exceeds its tortoise-fertility. **The monotonicity conjecture for exceptional-word ratios.** The numbers

$$
\frac{|\mathcal E_m|}{|\mathcal{NW}_m|}
$$

are increasing in $m$. The paper reports computed values for $m=7,8,9$ and observes that, if the conjecture holds, the limiting ratio exists; its value remains to be determined.

340619.title: Samotij's theorem analog for projective cubes in $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$

340907.title: The Alishahi–Dowlin spectral sequence conjecture from Khovanov homology to knot Floer homology
340907.literal_statement:
Let $K$ be a knot in $S^{3}$. The Khovanov homology of $K$ and the knot Floer homology of $K$ are the endpoints of a conjectural spectral sequence.

341123.title: Closed-form maximal Randić energy conjecture for selected orders

341255.title: Uniqueness of local moves preserving electrical equivalence in punctured-disk networks

341267.title: Sullivan's compromise conjectures for the second neighbourhood
341267.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be an oriented graph. For a vertex $x$ of $D$, write $d^{+}(x)$ and $d^{-}(x)$ for its out-degree and in-degree, respectively, and let $d^{++}(x)$ denote the number of vertices at directed distance exactly 2 from $x$.

**Sullivan's compromise conjectures.** Every oriented graph $D$ has a vertex $x$ satisfying at least one of the following two assertions:

$$
d^{++}(x)\geq d^{-}(x),
$$

or

$$
d^{++}(x)+d^{+}(x)\geq 2d^{-}(x).
$$

These are weaker alternatives to Seymour's Second Neighbourhood Conjecture. The source attributes them to Sullivan, but the supplied material does not establish whether either conjecture has been resolved.

Exact bit/set diagnostics are not Lean certificates.

341290.title: The final-matrix Sierpinski-triangle conjecture
341290.literal_statement:
Let $FM_n^{-}(x,y)$ be the negative final-matrix value and let $\mathrm{ST}_n$ be defined recursively by $\mathrm{ST}_0=(1,1)$ and

$$
(x,y)\in\mathrm{ST}_{n+1}\iff ((x)_{2^n},(y)_{2^n})\in\mathrm{ST}_n\text{ and }(x\leq2^n\text{ or }y>2^n).
$$

**Final-matrix Sierpinski-triangle conjecture.** Suppose $n\geq0$ and $\ell\leq x*y$ in $A_n$. Then:

1. If $M_n(x,y,\ell)>0$, then $(x*M_n(x,y,\ell),\ell)\in\mathrm{ST}_n$.
2. If $M_n(x,y,\ell)<0$, then $(-M_n(x,y,\ell),\ell)\in\mathrm{ST}_n$.

The claim formalizes the observed Sierpinski-triangle pattern in the final matrices, which the excerpt describes as unproved and important for understanding the combinatorial complexity of multigenic Laver tables.

Detailed range in laver9-results.json; no failing triple found. No Lean endpoint is claimed. Completed n=0 through 9; n=9 has order 512 and 112295936 admissible triples, all passing.

353295.title: Nonexistence conjecture for superlinear elliptic inequalities on weighted graphs
353295.literal_statement:
Let $(V,\b5)$ be a weighted graph, let $o\in V$, and let $\sigma>1$. A nonnegative solution $u$ of the elliptic inequality

$$
\Delta u+u^{\sigma}\leq 0
$$

is a function on $V$ satisfying this inequality, where $B(o,n)$ denotes the ball of radius $n$ centered at $o$ and $\mu(B(o,n))$ its weighted volume. **Nonexistence conjecture.** If

$$
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{n^{2\sigma-1}}{\mu(B(o,n))^{\sigma-1}}=\infty,
$$

then the only nonnegative solution to the elliptic inequality is identically zero. This would sharpen the stated nonexistence theorem by removing condition $(p_0)$, whose necessity is not known.

365811.title: Máčajová–Škoviera odd-cut conjecture for bridgeless cubic graphs
365811.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. A **perfect matching** is a set of edges meeting every vertex exactly once, and an **edge-cut** is the set of edges joining a vertex subset to its complement. **Máčajová–Škoviera conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph has two perfect matchings such that their intersection does not contain an edge-cut of odd cardinality. 366094.title: Merzon–Smirnov's layered-permutation conjecture for maximal Schubert specialization
366094.literal_statement:

A **layered permutation** $w(b_1,\ldots,b_k)$ is the concatenation of decreasing blocks on consecutive intervals, where $b_1+\cdots+b_k=n$. **Merzon–Smirnov's conjecture.** For $n\geq 1$, the permutations in $S_n$ attaining $\alpha_n$ are layered permutations. 372128.title: Nonnegativity conjecture for the summed edge-deletion gamma-polynomial
372128.literal_statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a 2-connected graph. For each edge $ij\in E$, set $c^{ij}(t):=h^*_{P_G}(t)-h^*_{P_{G\setminus ij}}(t)$, and let $\gamma(c^{ij}(t))$ denote the $\gamma$-polynomial associated with this palindromic difference. Define

$$
Z_G(t):=\sum_{ij\in E}\gamma(c^{ij}(t))=\sum_{ij\in E}\gamma\bigl(h^*_{P_G}(t)-h^*_{P_{G\setminus ij}}(t)\bigr)=\sum_{ij\in E}\bigl(\gamma_{P_G}(t)-\gamma_{P_{G\setminus ij}}(t)\bigr).
$$

**Summed edge-deletion nonnegativity conjecture.** The polynomial $Z_G(t)$ has nonnegative coefficients. This is proposed as a stronger statement whose gamma-nonnegativity would imply the existence of an edge with gamma-nonnegative deletion difference; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

335078.title: Distinct leverage centralities in Cartesian powers of path powers

335254.title: Aleksandrov–Buryak–Tessler conjecture for the extended refined partition function
335254.literal_statement:
Let $N$ be any value for which the formal series are defined, let $\tau^{o,\mathrm{ext}}_N$ be the extended refined open partition function, and let $\tau_N$ be the Kontsevich–Penner tau-function. Use the formal variables $t_i$ and $s_i$ and make the substitutions

$$
T_{2i+1}=\frac{t_i}{(2i+1)!!},\qquad T_{2i+2}=\frac{s_i}{2^{i+1}(i+1)!}.
$$

**Extended refined Kontsevich–Penner conjecture.** For any $N$ we have

$$
\tau^{o,\mathrm{ext}}_N=\left.\tau_N\right|_{\substack{T_{2i+1}=\frac{t_i}{(2i+1)!!},\\T_{2i+2}=\frac{s_i}{2^{i+1}(i+1)!}.}}
$$

The equality is known for $N=1$ and the source states that the conjecture is proved in genus $0$ and $1$; it remains open in general.
